1	/**
     2	 * variables.ts
     3	 *
     4	 * Pure template-engine function for resolving variable substitutions.
     5	 * Handles {{varName}} syntax. No file-system I/O.
     6	 */
     7	
     8	/**
     9	 * Resolve variable substitutions in a template string.
    10	 *
    11	 * Replaces `{{varName}}` markers with `String(context[varName])`.
    12	 * If a variable is not found in `context` (or its value is `undefined`),
    13	 * the original marker is preserved and a warning is emitted via
    14	 * `console.warn`, identifying the file by `filename` for easier debugging.
    15	 *
    16	 * **Escape syntax:** prefix a marker with a backslash (`\{{varName}}`) to
    17	 * emit the literal `{{varName}}` text in the output without performing any
    18	 * lookup or triggering an unresolved-variable warning.
    19	 *
    20	 * Note: this step must run AFTER `resolvePartials` and `resolveConditionals`
    21	 * so that only plain variable markers remain.
    22	 *
    23	 * @param text     - Template string potentially containing {{varName}} markers
    24	 * @param context  - Key-value map of variable name → value
    25	 * @param filename - Identifier used in warning messages (e.g. persona file path)
    26	 * @returns        The template string with variable markers substituted
    27	 */
    28	export function resolveVariables(
    29	  text: string,
    30	  context: Record<string, unknown>,
    31	  filename: string,
    32	): string {
    33	  return text.replace(/(\\?)\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (match, escape: string, varName: string) => {
    34	    if (escape === '\\') {
    35	      return `{{${varName}}}`;
    36	    }
    37	    if (varName in context && context[varName] !== undefined) {
    38	      return String(context[varName]);
    39	    }
    40	    console.warn(`[WARN] Unresolved variable: ${match} in ${filename}`);
    41	    return match;
    42	  });
    43	}

1	# AI Persona Builder
     2	
     3	Build AI persona instruction files for **VS Code Chat**, **Claude Code** and **LangGraph Deep Agents** from YAML metadata and Markdown templates — with zero configuration friction.
     4	
     5	Define your personas once as simple YAML + Markdown sources, and the library generates correctly formatted instruction files for both IDEs. A plugin system lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or post-process output without touching the core engine.
     6	
     7	## ✨ Features
     8	
     9	- **Multi-target output** — generates VS Code `.agent.md`, Claude Code `.md`, Deep Agents `.md`, and any custom format from a single source
    10	- **Extensible target registry** — register custom targets via `TargetRegistry` without touching core code; each target declares its own output key, frontmatter template, and context flags
    11	- **YAML + Markdown templating** — separate metadata from content; merge them at build time with `{{variables}}`, `{{> partials}}`, and `{{#if}}` conditionals
    12	- **Shared + per-suite partials** — reuse content fragments across personas with local overrides
    13	- **Custom variables** — inject global or per-suite template variables via `BuildConfig.variables` and `SuiteConfig.variables` without touching persona YAML files
    14	- **Dynamic partials** — supply inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`, or override them at suite or per-persona level through the `onPartials` and `onPersonaPartials` plugin hooks
    15	- **Plugin architecture** — hook into context building, post-rendering, validation, and frontmatter generation
    16	- **CI-friendly** — `--check` mode renders without writing; `--strict` exits non-zero on warnings
    17	- **Programmatic & CLI** — use the `build()` API in scripts or run `persona-build` from the command line
    18	- **Single dependency** — only `js-yaml` at runtime
    19	
    20	## 📋 Requirements
    21	
    22	- **Node.js** ≥ 18
    23	
    24	## 🚀 Quick Start
    25	
    26	```bash
    27	npm install @mistralys/persona-builder
    28	```
    29	
    30	- View on NPM: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mistralys/persona-builder
    31	- View on Github: https://github.com/Mistralys/ai-persona-builder
    32	
    33	### Programmatic API
    34	
    35	```ts
    36	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    37	import path from 'node:path';
    38	
    39	const summary = await build({
    40	  suites: {
    41	    'my-suite': {
    42	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
    43	      outputDirs: {
    44	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
    45	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
    46	      },
    47	    },
    48	  },
    49	  sharedPartialsDir: path.resolve('./personas/shared/partials'),
    50	});
    51	
    52	console.log(`Built ${summary.totalBuilt} persona(s), wrote ${summary.totalWritten} file(s).`);
    53	```
    54	
    55	### CLI
    56	
    57	```bash
    58	# Create a persona-build.config.js, then:
    59	npx persona-build
    60	
    61	# CI staleness check
    62	npx persona-build --check --strict
    63	```
    64	
    65	See the [CLI docs](docs/cli.md) for config file format and all flags.
    66	
    67	## 📖 Documentation
    68	
    69	**Guides** — conceptual and procedural reading:
    70	
    71	| Guide | Description |
    72	|-------|-------------|
    73	| [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) | Step-by-step tutorial — build your first persona from scratch |
    74	| [Directory Convention](docs/directory-convention.md) | Expected source layout (`meta/`, `content/`, `partials/`) |
    75	| [Template Syntax](docs/template-syntax.md) | Variables, partials, conditionals, and built-in context variables |
    76	| [Target Differences](docs/target-differences.md) | VS Code vs Claude Code — tool notation, frontmatter, filename conventions, and common mistakes |
    77	| [Custom Variables & Dynamic Partials](docs/dynamic-partials.md) | Inject build-time variables and partial content at global, suite, or per-persona level |
    78	| [Plugins](docs/plugins.md) | `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface and examples |
    79	
    80	**Reference** — look-up material:
    81	
    82	| Reference | Description |
    83	|-----------|-------------|
    84	| [Metadata Reference](docs/metadata-reference.md) | All recognized YAML metadata fields, tiers, and fallback rules |
    85	| [Configuration Reference](docs/configuration.md) | `BuildConfig`, `SuiteConfig`, and `BuildSummary` fields |
    86	| [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Command-line flags, config file format, and common patterns |
    87	| [Public API](docs/api.md) | All exported types and functions |
    88	| [Project Manifest](docs/agents/project-manifest/README.md) | Canonical documentation for AI agent sessions |
    89	
    90	## 🔌 Plugins
    91	
    92	The library ships with a plugin system that lets you inject custom frontmatter, run validators, or
    93	post-process output without touching the core engine. See [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md) for
    94	the `PersonaBuildPlugin` interface, examples, and the available hooks.
    95	
    96	> **Ledger plugin:** The first-party ledger plugin was migrated out of this library in v2.0.0 and
    97	> is now maintained in the [ai-insights](https://github.com/mistralys/ai-insights-dev) workspace.
    98	> The `@mistralys/persona-builder/plugins/ledger` sub-path export no longer exists.
    99

1	# Template Syntax
     2	
     3	Templates use a lightweight `{{…}}` syntax with no external dependencies.
     4	
     5	## Variables
     6	
     7	```
     8	{{variableName}}
     9	```
    10	
    11	Values are sourced from the merged context built in this priority order (later layers win):
    12	
    13	1. `BuildConfig.variables` — global defaults set in your top-level config
    14	2. `SuiteConfig.variables` — suite-level overrides
    15	3. `_shared.yaml` fields
    16	4. Per-persona YAML fields
    17	5. Derived/computed fields (e.g. `version`, `tools_list`)
    18	6. Cross-suite agent map (`agent_<slug>` variables)
    19	7. Target flags (`target_<name>` booleans) — always highest priority
    20	
    21	Plugin `onBuildContext` hooks run after step 4 and may contribute additional keys or override existing ones. Missing variables emit a warning to stderr but do not fail the build.
    22	
    23	## Partials
    24	
    25	```
    26	{{> partialName}}
    27	```
    28	
    29	Partials are loaded from the `partials/` directory and resolved up to 2 levels deep.
    30	
    31	## Conditionals
    32	
    33	```
    34	{{#if flagName}}
    35	Content shown when flagName is truthy.
    36	{{else}}
    37	Fallback content.
    38	{{/if}}
    39	```
    40	
    41	### Else-If Chains
    42	
    43	Use `{{else if flagName}}` to express multi-branch conditionals without deep nesting:
    44	
    45	```
    46	{{#if a}}
    47	Content shown when a is truthy.
    48	{{else if b}}
    49	Content shown when a is falsy and b is truthy.
    50	{{else}}
    51	Fallback content when both a and b are falsy.
    52	{{/if}}
    53	```
    54	
    55	**Truth table:**
    56	
    57	| `a` | `b` | Output |
    58	|-----|-----|--------|
    59	| `true` | any | first branch |
    60	| `false` | `true` | second branch |
    61	| `false` | `false` | `{{else}}` fallback |
    62	
    63	Chains may have any number of `{{else if}}` branches. The first truthy branch wins;
    64	all subsequent branches are discarded. If no branch is truthy and there is no
    65	`{{else}}`, the entire block is removed from the output.
    66	
    67	`{{else if}}` chains are normalised into equivalent nested `{{#if}}` blocks before
    68	resolution, so they compose correctly with traditional nested syntax.
    69	
    70	### Nested Conditionals
    71	
    72	`{{#if}}` blocks may be nested inside `{{else}}` branches. This is the standard pattern
    73	for writing content that differs across all three built-in targets:
    74	
    75	```
    76	{{#if target_vscode}}
    77	Content shown only in VS Code builds.
    78	{{else}}
    79	{{#if target_deep_agents}}
    80	Content shown only in Deep Agents builds.
    81	{{else}}
    82	Content shown in Claude Code (or any remaining) builds.
    83	{{/if}}
    84	{{/if}}
    85	```
    86	
    87	The engine resolves nested blocks innermost-first across multiple passes until the output
    88	stabilises. No stray `{{/if}}` markers appear in the output regardless of nesting depth.
    89	
    90	## Built-in Context Variables
    91	
    92	The builder automatically derives several convenience variables from YAML metadata:
    93	
    94	| Variable | Source |
    95	|----------|--------|
    96	| `{{version}}` | `version` field, or `default_version` from `_shared.yaml`, or `'0.0.0'` |
    97	| `{{tools_list}}` | Comma-separated string of `tools` array items |
    98	| `{{tools_json}}` | JSON array string of `tools` items |
    99	| `{{tools_block}}` | YAML block sequence of `tools` items; or ` []` when empty |
   100	| `{{cc_tools_list}}` | Comma-separated string of `cc_tools` (falls back to `tools`) |

    12

    23	### Escape Syntax
    24	
    25	Prefix a variable marker with a backslash to emit it as literal text, bypassing substitution and suppressing any unresolved-variable warning:
    26	
    27	```
    28	\{{variableName}}
    29	```
    30	
    31	The backslash is consumed by the engine; the output is the bare `{{variableName}}` marker with no substitution performed. This is useful when you need to show template syntax examples inside rendered output, or when you intentionally want to defer resolution to a downstream processor.
    32	
    33	**Double-backslash chaining:** The escape is applied to exactly one leading backslash. A double backslash (`\\{{variableName}}`) produces `\{{variableName}}` in the output — the first backslash acts as the escape character, and the second backslash passes through literally. This behaviour is consistent with standard template-engine escape chaining.
    34	
    35	| Input | Output |
    36	|-------|--------|
    37	| `\{{name}}` | `{{name}}` (literal, no substitution) |
    38	| `\\{{name}}` | `\{{name}}` (one backslash + literal marker) |
    39	| `{{name}}` | `Alice` (normal substitution, given `name = "Alice"`) |
    40

    42	
    43	```
    44	{{> partialName}}
    45	```
